Abstract base class representing a parameter range. Provides a factory (create) to instantiate a specific Range subclass from a string specification and a pure-virtual contains() to test whether a Parameter value lies within the range. Destruction is virtual to allow polymorphic deletion. Details of parsing and subclasses are defined in this header.
Concrete Range that accepts any Parameter value. contains() should always return true. No data members; behavior is unconditional inclusion.

Range representing a numeric interval parsed from a string (e.g., likely supporting open/closed bounds). Stores presence of lower/upper bounds, inclusivity flags, and the numeric boundary values using Real. contains() tests whether the Parameter value falls within the configured interval. Constructor parses the string specification. Exact format and validation rules are not shown here.

Range representing membership in a finite set parsed from a string specification. Stores the set of allowed string elements; contains() checks if the Parameter matches one of them. The test() method likely performs internal validation or diagnostics. Exact parsing format is not provided here.

Variant-like configuration/value holder class supporting multiple scalar, vector, matrix, and map parameter types used throughout Essentia. It stores the active type via ParamType and the value in corresponding members. Provides constructors from many C++ types, conversion accessors, comparison, and string formatting. Memory ownership: owns dynamically allocated child Parameters stored in _vec and _map; destructor and clear() free them. Unknowns: exact behavior of copy/move, destruction, and exceptions depend on definitions in the corresponding .cpp; however, interface implies deep copies and exception throwing on type/usage errors.

Input-side IO wrapper for Essentia standard algorithms. Inherits TypeProxy to enforce runtime type compatibility and stores a pointer to input data (single token or token vector) coming from a streaming::SinkBase. It is owned/managed by an Algorithm and provides helpers to bind to sinks or set data directly via the templated set method (defined in iotypewrappers_impl.h). Construction/destruction specifics beyond default constructor are not exposed here.

Output-side IO wrapper for Essentia standard algorithms. Inherits TypeProxy to enforce runtime type compatibility and stores a pointer to output data (single token or token vector) provided by a streaming::SourceBase. It is owned/managed by an Algorithm and provides helpers to bind to sources or set data directly via the templated set method (defined in iotypewrappers_impl.h). Construction/destruction specifics beyond default constructor are not exposed here.

Concrete class representing a high-level streaming connector in Essentia. Inherits from TypeProxy (to carry runtime type information of the data flowing through it) and StreamConnector (connection mechanics). Maintains an owning/non-owning pointer to its parent Algorithm and provides helpers to access parent and derive names. Construction is via provided constructors; destruction follows normal C++ rules (no custom destructor present). Details of TypeProxy and StreamConnector are external to this header.

Abstract base class for stream endpoints used by Essentia’s streaming framework. It models token-based flow control: querying availability, acquiring (consuming) tokens, and releasing (producing) tokens. It holds configurable default acquire/release sizes and requires derived classes to implement availability, acquire(n), release(n), and reset(). Construction is trivial; destruction is virtual; copying semantics are unspecified. Derived implementations must manage token buffers and enforce bounds (e.g., acquire should fail/return false if insufficient tokens).
A no-op mutex used when multithreading is disabled or unnecessary. Its lock/unlock do nothing, providing minimal overhead synchronization placeholders.
A no-op RAII-style locker for Mutex. Its constructor and methods perform no real locking; intended to mirror API of a real locker while incurring no synchronization cost.
A real mutex that always enforces mutual exclusion. On Windows it wraps CRITICAL_SECTION; on POSIX systems it wraps pthread_mutex_t and may throw EssentiaException if initialization fails.
RAII locker for ForcedMutex. Locks in the constructor and unlocks in the destructor to ensure exception-safe locking.

Abstract base class for Essentia standard algorithms. It derives from Configurable and provides registration and access to typed inputs/outputs via OrderedMap wrappers, lifecycle methods (compute as pure virtual and reset), and type introspection helpers. Concrete algorithms subclass Algorithm, declare inputs/outputs using declareInput/declareOutput, and implement compute. Ownership semantics and construction details are not specified in this header.

Do not manually unlock the same mutex while the locker is alive; unlocking is handled by the locker’s destructor.
Avoid copying/moving (not defined here); keep lifetime scoped to the critical section.

functions.name: essentia::ForcedMutexLocker::~ForcedMutexLocker
functions.description: Destructor that unlocks the associated ForcedMutex acquired during construction.
requirements: The associated ForcedMutex must still be valid at destruction time.
Do not destroy the ForcedMutex before the locker is destroyed.

functions.description: Adds a Real value under the given descriptor name. Multiple calls with the same name append to that descriptor’s vector of values. If validityCheck is true, a NaN/Inf check is performed and an exception is thrown on invalid data. Throws if name conflicts with an existing namespace (i.e., name has children). Do not mix types under the same descriptor name.

The descriptor identified by name must either be new or already store Real values added via add; mixing types under the same name is not allowed.
If validityCheck == true, value must be finite (no NaN/Inf) or an exception is thrown.

Callers must respect Pool’s locking order if manually locking across public mutexes: mutexReal, mutexVectorReal, mutexString, mutexVectorString, mutexArray2DReal, mutexStereoSample, mutexSingleReal, mutexSingleString, mutexSingleVectorReal, mutexSingleVectorString, mutexTensorReal, mutexSingleTensorReal.
Do not rely on set() semantics for add(): add always appends to the internal vector for that name.

functions.description: Performance-oriented utility to append a batch of values into the vector for a descriptor name. Unlike add(), this assumes the descriptor already maps to a vector container of the exact same element type and may fail in subtle ways if misused. Only specialized for certain T; the generic template throws an EssentiaException at runtime.
requirements: Only the following specializations are implemented: T=Real, T=std::vector<Real>, T=std::string, T=std::vector<std::string>, T=StereoSample. For any other T, this function throws EssentiaException("Pool::append not implemented for type: ...").
If name already exists with the correct vector element type, values are appended; otherwise, the function initializes that entry with values after validating the key (validateKey).
Do not mix types under the same descriptor name.
Caller should prefer add() unless performance considerations and exact type/shape are guaranteed.
If locking manually, follow the documented mutex lock order.

Respect mutex locking order if locking externally.

functions.name: essentia::db2pow

functions.name: essentia::amp2db

functions.name: essentia::db2amp

functions.name: essentia::bark2hz

functions.name: essentia::mel2hzSlaney

functions.name: essentia::hz2melSlaney

tuningFrequency > 0
